references.text: Deuteronomy repeats the prohibition against dishonest weights and measures, emphasizing that such actions are an abomination to the Lord.
Proverbs confirms that a false weight is an abomination to the Lord, while accurate weights please him.
Proverbs teaches that just weights and balances come from the Lord.
Proverbs warns against using two kinds of weights and two kinds of measures, which are an abomination to the Lord.
Ezekiel repeats the requirement for just weights, with the ephah and the bath as standard measures in restored Israel.
Amos condemns those who make the ephah small and the shekel large, and who use dishonest scales.
Micah condemns unjust measures and false weights as part of Israel's sin.
